newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Goias state to auction power plant Sept 5.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Goias state to auction power plant Sept 5.

text.p: The first privatization of a Brazilian power generator will take place Sept. 5 with the auction of the Cachoeira Dourada hydroelectric plant owned by Goias state, a planning official said Monday.

A base price of 543.4 million reais ($503.1 million) has been set for a 78.9 percent stake in the 658-megawatt power plant, which is to be sold in a closed-envelope auction on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange, the official said.
The state is also offering 1.78 percent of the capital to the plant's employees at a 20 percent discount.
Goias state currently owns 98 percent of Cachoeira Dourada's voting capital and 70 percent of preference shares, or the equivalent of 80.68 percent of total capital.

The new controlling shareholders will have to pay the full auction price in cash by September 12. Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), which oversees the privatization process, is offering to finance 50 percent of the minimum price, the official said. No privatization bonds will be accepted as payment.
Investors interested in obtaining the BNDES financing have to apply by August 6.
The new controlling shareholders will also have until September 15 to pay of 45 million reais ($41.7 million) of debt that Cachoeira Dourada owes the state, the official said.

Investors will have to "pre-qualify" for the auction between August 8 and August 25, with an announcement of those making the cut by August 29. Pre-qualifiers will have to deposit financial guarantees with the Rio stock exchange clearing house between August 29 and September 3.
Cachoeira Dourada was set up in November 1996 when Goias state spun off the generating arm of Centrais Electricas de Goias (Celg), which now mainly involved in power distribution.

About 20 companies have shown interest in acquiring Cachoeira Dourada, including Electricite de France, Belgium's Tractebel SA and Chile's Empresa Nacional de Electricidad SA, or Endesa. Three U.S. companies have shown interest -- NationsBank Corp, Houston Industries Inc and AES Corp -- as well as Japan's Marubeni Corp and Brazil's Votorantim Inc, Bradesco SA and Camargo Correa SA.
